main_text.l: similarium & difsimilarium actiones non
differre, si omnes nostri corporis partes ita
agunt, sicut struthiocameli uenter, cuius
actio semper est uniuoca. Quantum autem
inter se discrepent omniū nostri corporis
partium actiones, iudicent medicinæ ty-
rones. Nam quemadmodum actionum læ-
sio est duplex, quarum una ad animalem, al-
tera ad naturalem functionem pertinet: ita
duplices numerantur actiones, naturalis ui-
delicet, & animalis, quemadmodum often
dit Galenus libro de Differentijs sympto-
matum. His adde quòd tot sunt actionum
differentiæ, quot sunt nostri corporis par-
tium genera. At alias esse similares, alias dis-
similares & compositas nemine medicum
latet. Quamuis similares partes intellexe-
rit, quibus solis uis alimentum concoquen-
di & assimilandi sit, non tamen ipsum ali-
mentum pariter coficiunt. Longè enim ali-
ter hepar & uenæ coquunt, quàm uentricu-
lus & uenæ portæ. Deinde postrema con-
coctio, quæ quidem in habitu corporis per-
agitur, & assimilatio ab aliis alimenti mu-
tationibus non parum inter se discrepant.

page.notes: The word "often" in the line "quemadmodum often dit Galenus" is printed as "often" in the scan, reading "quemadmodum osten" is not clear; the printed word appears to be "often" with a long-s spelling "ofte" and is uncertain. Lines are rendered as paragraph flow; the hyphenated line-end words "concoc-tio" appear as "concoctio" and "pera-gitur" as "peragitur" in the printing. The printed line ending "stru-" continues on the next page as "thio-". The right-margin word "thio-" is a catchword-like continuation and is kept as a note. Text "alimenti mutationibus" and "uentriculus" read as printed. Two printing irregularities: "uenter, cuius" at the start and "uenæ" repeated are as printed; no corrections applied.
